newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli provident funds post outflow in February.
newsitem.headline: Israeli provident funds post outflow in February.

text.p: Net redemptions in Israeli provident funds reached 222 million shekels in February bringing total withdrawals for the year to 489 million shekels, Israel's Finance Ministry said on Monday.

In 1996, the provident funds suffered net redemptions of 11.7 billion shekels although in December they enjoyed a rare net inflow of 397 million shekels. Savers traditionally put money into the funds at the end of the year for tax reasons.
Provident funds are long-term savings schemes that invest most of their assets in Treasury bonds.
The Treasury also said savings programmes suffered net withdrawals for February of 509 million shekels, bringing total withdrawals for 1997 to 574 million shekels.
Inflation-linked savings schemes experienced a 450 million shekel drop. They had had an increase in January of 19 million shekels.
Banking sources attributed the withdrawals to falling interest rates.
Savings programmes had been the recipients of deposits in the last two years, taking in a total of 5.36 billion shekels last year alone.
